easy.q: To whom is the psalm attributed in its heading?

easy.q: For what does the psalmist’s soul long and faint?

answers: Those who dwell in God’s house
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Blessed are they that dwell in thy house.”

medium.q: How does the psalmist describe his desire for the Lord’s dwelling?

answers: They have found a home and a nest there

answers: His longing involves his whole person
His longing has turned into anger

challenge.q: What is the result for those who dwell in God’s house?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Blessed is the man whose strength is in thee.”
easy.q: In whom does the blessed man find his strength?

easy.explanation: They “make it a well,” according to the KJV.
easy.q: What do those passing through the valley of Baca make?

easy.q: Where does every one of them appear before God?

answers: The ways of the Lord’s people
medium.explanation: The verse says, “in whose heart are the ways of them.”
medium.q: What is written in the heart of the blessed man?

answers: It becomes a well and is filled with pools

paragraphs.title: A Prayer for the Protector and the Anointed King

easy.explanation: The prayer begins, “O LORD God of hosts, hear my prayer.”
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist direct his prayer?

answers: Hear and give ear to his prayer
easy.explanation: He asks, “hear my prayer: give ear” to him.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do?

easy.explanation: He asks God to “look upon the face of thine anointed.”
easy.q: Upon whose face does the psalmist ask God to look?

medium.explanation: The prayer says, “give ear, O God of Jacob.”
medium.q: What additional title is given to the LORD in the prayer?

medium.explanation: The word “shield” portrays God as the protector of His people.
medium.q: What does “our shield” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: The psalmist first asks God to hear and give ear, then to look upon the anointed.
medium.q: What is the order of the requests in the prayer?

answers: The psalmist asks God both to protect and to watch over His people’s ruler
The psalmist asks God to withdraw from the ruler
The psalmist asks someone else to replace the shield
challenge.explanation: God is called their shield, and the prayer asks Him to give attentive care to the anointed.
challenge.q: What connection exists between “our shield” and the request to “look upon” the anointed?

answers: The prayer includes God’s care for the anointed king
The anointed is described as abandoning God
The anointed is said to replace God
challenge.explanation: The anointed represents the king who is to receive God’s attention and protection.
challenge.q: Why is the anointed mentioned along with the request for God’s protection?

answers: A repeated appeal for God’s attention
A declaration that no answer is needed
A description of a wilderness journey
challenge.explanation: The repeated commands emphasize the psalmist’s earnest request for God to listen and act.
challenge.q: What feature of prayer is emphasized by “hear,” “give ear,” and “look”?

paragraphs.title: The Goodness of God’s House and Trust in the Lord

answers: One day in the LORD’s courts
One day in the tents of wickedness

easy.q: How is the LORD described in verse 11?

answers: The person who trusts in the LORD
The person who lives among the wicked
easy.explanation: The psalm concludes, “blessed is the man that trusteth in thee.”
easy.q: Who is called blessed at the end of the psalm?

answers: Being a doorkeeper in the house of his God
Returning to the valley of Baca

A house, a nest, and a well
